dossier.summary: Pinecrest Mutual is a regional auto and home insurer with about 320 staff and policyholders in four states.
dossier.why_now: Named a new VP of Claims in August.

notes.title: Call notes, Oct 22: Pinecrest Mutual claims intake
notes.text:
Thursday October 22, 2026, 30 min, phone. Pinecrest: Robert Kaminski (VP Claims), Dana Oyelowo (Claims Operations Lead), Luis Ferreira (IT Director). Northfield: Elena Marsh, Theo Brandt (Implementation Lead).

About 38,000 auto and home claims a year. First notice of loss comes in by phone (about 70 percent) and a web form (the rest). The web form writes into the claims system, which dates from 2009. A phone intake takes 22 minutes on average; Dana measured it in September. Adjusters re-key the photos policyholders email in. Policyholders call back to ask for status because there is no status page or text.

Robert wants: photo upload at first notice, status texts, and a shorter phone intake. Not replacing the core system this year.

Luis: the core system has no live API. It takes a batch file nightly. Anything we do has to work with the nightly batch. He wants a technical review before any proposal.

Agreed: Northfield runs a technical review with Luis's team on Wednesday November 4. Pinecrest shares a sample of 50 anonymized claims by Friday October 30 so Theo can map the fields. Northfield sends a proposal scoped to auto claims only by Thursday November 12. Robert takes it to the Q4 operations review on Thursday December 3. Dana sends the September intake timing report (no date given).

Resources: Northfield integration guide (https://northfield.example/docs/integration-guide.pdf), call recording (https://northfield.example/rec/pinecrest-oct-22).

notes.title: Transcript, Oct 22 call (auto)
notes.text:
[00:02:10] Robert Kaminski: We are not replacing the core system this year. I want to fix the front door: how a claim comes in and what the policyholder hears afterwards.
[00:06:45] Dana Oyelowo: I timed phone intakes in September. Twenty-two minutes on average. A lot of that is the adjuster typing while the caller looks for the policy number.
[00:12:30] Luis Ferreira: Whatever you build has to feed the nightly batch. There is no live API and there will not be one before next year.
[00:13:02] Theo Brandt: Understood. If you can share a sample of claims with the personal details removed, I can map the fields before we talk again.
[00:13:20] Luis Ferreira: Fifty claims, anonymized, by the end of the month.
[00:24:15] Robert Kaminski: Scope it to auto first. Home claims have a different intake and I do not want to fight two battles.
[00:25:00] Elena Marsh: Auto only, proposal by the twelfth, and Luis gets the technical review before that.
[00:25:10] Robert Kaminski: Then I take it to the ops review on December 3.
